basic_identification.full_title: Builder's Hoist — Specification (First Revision) (बिल्डर्स होईस्ट — विशिष्टि (पहला पुनरीक्षण))
basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering / Construction Plant and Machinery (approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Construction Plant and Machinery Sectional Committee, MED 18, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Construction Plant and Machinery Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the general requirements for construction, safety, capacity, performance, and testing of builder's hoists (platform hoists with or without tilting buckets) used for the vertical transport of building materials during construction or refurbishment operations.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification / Safety and Performance Code (Mechanical Engineering Department / Construction Machinery)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to carry the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' on the manufacturer's nameplate. Compliance with IS 12466:2012 is legally mandatory under State Public Works Department (PWD) specifications, central construction safety guidelines, municipal building bylaws, and public/private infrastructure supply tenders across India.

requirements.detail: Builder's hoists under this standard are defined specifically as platform hoists with or without a tilting bucket, and the standard explicitly excludes any other passenger-carrying or heavy industrial crane hoists.
The hoist unit must comprise three integrated mechanical assemblies: (a) a winch unit, (b) a mast or masts, and (c) a platform or platforms with or without a tilting bucket.

The capacity of the builder's hoist must be designated in terms of safe working loads (excluding the weight of the platform or bucket) strictly matching standard ranges: 0.25T, 0.5T, 0.75T, and 1T (Tonnes) at a vertical speed of 0.3 m/s to 0.5 m/s.
Electric-driven winches must utilize three-phase induction motors conforming to IS 325. Fuel-driven variants must utilize constant-speed diesel engines conforming to IS 10001 (not exceeding 20 kW).
The hoisting cables must utilize high-tensile steel wire ropes conforming to IS 2266, aligned and maintained in accordance with the rope safety guidelines of IS 3973.
All raw structural steel sections utilized to manufacture the main mast columns, base plates, and structural connections must conform to IS 2062.

The hoist must be equipped with an automatic power-fail-safe brake motor and a positive mechanical safety braking system attached to the carriage to immediately lock the platform to the mast in the event of wire rope failure.

Upper and lower ultimate limit switches must be structurally integrated into the travel path of the platform carriage to cut mechanical power and prevent over-travel or crashing at the top or bottom of the mast.

To prevent structural buckling or swaying, the vertical mast must be rigidly secured to the building facade or support columns using wall ties at regular vertical intervals (typically every 6 meters).

All observed or calculated test and performance values (including safe loads, speeds, and clearances) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 12466 : 2012 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification establishing technical, material, structural, and safety requirements for builder's hoists (platform hoists with or without tilting buckets) used to transport raw building materials vertically on construction sites. Maintained under the Construction Plant and Machinery Sectional Committee (MED 18) and reaffirmed in 2022, the standard unifies hoist engineering and operations in India. It defines standardized lifting capacities (0.25T, 0.5T, 0.75T, and 1T) at speeds ranging from 0.3 m/s to 0.5 m/s, regulates raw material properties (such as IS 2062 structural steel and IS 2266 wire ropes), and mandates critical safety devices—including automatic fail-safe power brakes, mechanical wire-rope-break carriage locks, upper/lower limit switches, and rigid 6-meter wall tie anchorages—to eliminate catastrophic on-site collapse and fall hazards.
